deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the draft of the second part of Riemann's Paris prize essay (Commentatio mathematica, 1861), which sits in the heat-conduction bundle. The previous page chose coordinates at a point O with a_{ιι'}(O) normalised and first derivatives zero (eq. 5), plus the symmetries (6) and (7) of the second derivatives. In such coordinates, and when all second-order variations ddx, dδx, δδx vanish, the expansion of the metric near O is eq. 8: ds² = ds0² + (2/3) Σ ∂²a_{ιι'}/∂x_{ι''}∂x_{ι'''} · (dx_ι δx_{ι''} − δx_ι dx_{ι''})(dx_{ι'} δx_{ι'''} − δx_{ι'} dx_{ι'''}). Those conditions depend on the coordinates, so on this page Riemann recasts them in a form valid for arbitrary variables.

(a) Replacing (5) and (6). Riemann now imposes the invariant relations
  dd Σ a δxδx = δδ Σ a dx dx = −2 dδ Σ a dx δx.
The first expression is written dd Σ a dx dx on the page; it should be dd Σ a δxδx. In the special coordinates both equalities follow from (6) and (7), using dδx = 0 and so on (my filling). Writing X = dd Σ a δxδx, Y = dδ Σ a dx δx and Z = δδ Σ a dx dx, the relations give X = Z = −2Y. Hence X = (X − 2Y + Z)/3, which is eq. 9: the curvature term equals one third of the symmetric combination X − 2Y + Z.

(b) Replacing ∂a(O) = 0 and the vanishing of second variations. Let δ' be an arbitrary third variation, with all variations commuting. In the special coordinates the three expansions written on the page hold: δ'Σ a dx δx = Σ a dδ'x δx + Σ a dx δδ'x, and similarly for the other two. Subtracting them gives eq. 10:
  δ'(Σ a dx δx) − d(Σ a δ'x δx) − δ(Σ a dx δ'x) = 0.
Setting d = δ gives eq. 11, which is the first variation of Σ a dx dx (the Euler–Lagrange or geodesic condition) in both directions.

Equation 10 contains no coordinate-dependent assumption. Expanding it in general coordinates (my filling) gives
  −Σ_ν δ'x_ν [2 Σ_ι a_{νι} dδx_ι + Σ p_{νιι'} dx_ι δx_{ι'}] = 0,
where p_{νιι'} = ∂a_{νι}/∂x_{ι'} + ∂a_{νι'}/∂x_ι − ∂a_{ιι'}/∂x_ν, i.e. twice the Christoffel symbol of the first kind. Since δ' is arbitrary, this yields the three second-order relations on the page: 2Σ a_{νι} ddx_ι = −Σ p_{νιι'} dx dx, 2Σ a_{νι} dδx_ι = −Σ p_{νιι'} dx δx, and 2Σ a_{νι} δδx_ι = −Σ p_{νιι'} δx δx. These are the parallel-transport / geodesic second variations.

(c) The invariant curvature form. Substituting these second variations into X − 2Y + Z gives the coordinate-free quadrilinear form
  Σ (ιι', ι''ι''') (dx_ι δx_{ι'} − δx_ι dx_{ι'})(dx_{ι''} δx_{ι'''} − δx_{ι''} dx_{ι'''}).
Here (ιι', ι''ι''') is Riemann's four-index symbol, i.e. the covariant Riemann curvature tensor: second derivatives of a plus quadratic terms in p contracted with the inverse metric. Its explicit form is not written here; it appears in the published Commentatio. Riemann calls this form the measure of curvature of the general space.

(d) Normalisation. With ds² = Σ a dx dx, δs² = Σ a δxδx and cos ϑ = Σ a dx δx/(ds δs), the infinitesimal triangle spanned by ds and δs has area Δ = ½ ds δs sin ϑ. Hence 4Δ² = (Σ a dx dx)(Σ a δxδx) − (Σ a dx δx)², the Gram determinant. Riemann rewrites this as (1/4) Σ over all index quadruples of (a_{ιι'} a_{ι''ι'''} − a_{ιι'''} a_{ι'ι''}) times the two bivector factors. The page breaks off just before the quotient: curvature form divided by 4Δ², up to a constant factor. This is the sectional curvature in the plane spanned by dx and δx.
errors: Line 1 of the displayed equations: the left side reads dd Σ a dx dx; it must be dd Σ a δx δx, as on the previous page. This is a slip of the pen or of the transcription; eq. 9 likewise needs δxδx in its first term.

The three expansions under 'Reliquas conditiones' omit the first-derivative terms. They are valid only in the special coordinates where ∂a = 0 at O and dδx = 0. This is intended, but the text does not say so.

In the 4Δ² identity, the second product must be the antisymmetrising partner a_{ιι'''} a_{ι'ι''} for the factor 1/4 over all quadruples to be right. The transcribed a_{ιι''} a_{ι'ι'''} contracts to zero against the bivector and would give a factor 1/2 instead. The image appears to read a_{ι'ι''} a_{ιι'''}, so this is probably a transcription error.
In the second-order relations, p carries only two indices (p_{ιι'}); it should be p_{νιι'}. This is a transcription or notational shorthand.
The second line under eq. 10 is transcribed as δdδ'x; it should read dδ'x.

results.what: Invariant (coordinate-free) characterisation of normal-coordinate conditions via the variational identity (10) and the geodesic equations (11)
results.modern_name: Geodesic equations / parallel transport via Christoffel symbols of the first kind
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Commentatio 1861, published 1876); Christoffel 1869 for the symbols

results.what: Curvature quadrilinear form (ιι',ι''ι''') contracted with two bivectors, arising from dd − 2dδ + δδ
Normalisation by the area of the infinitesimal triangle, 4Δ² = Gram determinant

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of the Commentatio mathematica (1861), whose content (the Riemann tensor symbol and sectional curvature) was published in the 1876 Werke and is famously Riemann's. Only minor draft variants are new.
